cases.prompt: Our Express controllers have grown huge, with tax calculation and discount rules right inside the route handlers. Where should that business logic actually live?
expectations: States the Dependency Rule: source code dependencies point inward toward higher-level policies
Recommends moving the business rules out of controllers into Use Case Interactors
Says controllers should only translate the delivery mechanism into Use Case input and delegate
Keeps the entity/use-case logic testable without HTTP or a database

cases.prompt: Should our business code call the web framework, or should the framework be calling our code? I keep hearing the phrase 'the framework is a detail.'
expectations: Explains the framework must call inward; business code must not import or depend on the framework
Places frameworks and drivers in the outermost circle as replaceable details
Mentions dependency inversion (interfaces defined inward, implemented outward) as the mechanism
Describes Main/composition root wiring concrete implementations together

cases.prompt: We want to move from Postgres to DynamoDB, but our ActiveRecord models are used directly everywhere in the domain code. How do we decouple?
expectations: Warns against ORM models leaking into business logic / entities not being database rows
Introduces a repository interface (e.g. UserRepository) defined by the inner circle and implemented in the adapters layer
States that DTOs, not ORM entities, cross the boundary
Isolates persistence in outer-circle gateways/adapters so the database can be swapped without touching business rules

cases.prompt: Should we split our app into microservices? Everyone says microservices are better architecture.
expectations: Counters that microservices are not automatically good architecture
Warns that a microservice with a fat shared data model is a distributed monolith
Frames services as deployment boundaries, not architectural boundaries
Says the Dependency Rule must apply within and across services

cases.prompt: Component A imports from Component B and Component B imports back from Component A, and each build keeps breaking the other. How do we fix this?
expectations: Identifies the cycle as a violation of the Acyclic Dependencies Principle (ADP)
Recommends applying DIP to invert a dependency edge or extracting a new shared component to break the cycle
Mentions the component coupling principles (ADP/SDP/SAP) governing component relationships
Explains the goal of keeping releases independent and changes localized
